transcript.text: Good evening everyone. I've called this meeting to close out the Bay 4 hydrogen alarm incident so we can get overnight charging capacity lined up. As we all know, Bay 4 had a hydrogen alarm during the afternoon shift; the alarm has since reset and there's no visible damage, but we need charging capacity for six forklifts tonight. I can authorize Bay 2 for temporary use since it's available and normally reserved for maintenance vehicles. Before I can authorize that, per our incident-closeout routine, I need to hear a facilities maintenance report and an EHS report. Once I've heard both, I'll record the operating plan, assign follow-up actions, and then we can proceed. Could I please get the facilities maintenance report first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I inspected Bay 4 after the alarm and found that the exhaust-fan belt has failed. The replacement belt is on site, but fitting and testing it will take exactly 6 hours. I haven't entered the emergency work order yet because the maintenance system was offline during the inspection.

transcript.text: Thanks, Eli. I have the EHS report ready. My same-day EHS review found that the Bay 4 alarm was caused by hydrogen accumulation. I also need to flag two important findings for the operating plan: First, Bay 2 is approved for no more than 4 simultaneous forklift chargers, not 6, so we'll need a plan for the remaining two forklifts. Second, our charging policy requires a 2-hour fire watch and a gas test showing less than 1% hydrogen before any charging can resume. I haven't attached my review to the incident record yet because the shift handover is still open, but I'm disclosing these findings now so they can inform the operating plan and follow-up actions.
